
ADD-DEPENDENCY
Add dependency relationships between work units to track blockers and dependencies

USAGE
  fspec add-dependency <id> [dependsOnId] [options]

ARGUMENTS
  <id> (required)
    Work unit ID to add dependency to
  [dependsOnId] (optional)
    Work unit ID that this depends on (shorthand for --depends-on)

OPTIONS
  --blocks <id>
    This work unit blocks the specified work unit
  --blocked-by <id>
    This work unit is blocked by the specified work unit
  --depends-on <id>
    This work unit depends on the specified work unit
  --relates-to <id>
    This work unit is related to the specified work unit (no blocking)

EXAMPLES
  1. Shorthand: AUTH-002 depends on AUTH-001
  $ fspec add-dependency AUTH-002 AUTH-001
  ✓ Added dependency: AUTH-002 depends on AUTH-001

  2. AUTH-002 blocks API-001 from starting
  $ fspec add-dependency AUTH-002 --blocks API-001
  ✓ Added dependency: AUTH-002 blocks API-001

  3. UI-001 is blocked by API-001
  $ fspec add-dependency UI-001 --blocked-by API-001
  ✓ Added dependency: UI-001 blocked by API-001

  4. Explicit: DASH-001 depends on AUTH-001
  $ fspec add-dependency DASH-001 --depends-on AUTH-001
  ✓ Added dependency: DASH-001 depends on AUTH-001

  5. UI-005 is related to UI-004 (no blocking)
  $ fspec add-dependency UI-005 --relates-to UI-004
  ✓ Added dependency: UI-005 relates to UI-004

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Work unit AUTH-999 not found
    Fix: Verify the work unit ID exists with: fspec list-work-units

  ✗ Circular dependency detected
    Fix: Remove the circular dependency chain before adding this relationship

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec remove-dependency
  fspec dependencies
  fspec export-dependencies
  fspec clear-dependencies

NOTES
  • Use shorthand syntax (two arguments) for simple depends-on relationships
  • Use explicit flags (--blocks, --depends-on) for clarity in complex dependency graphs
  • Circular dependencies are not allowed and will be rejected
